title: Three Weeks and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 语言文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）
meta: 主题语境：语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）　|　核心词汇：letter　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 letter 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the clerk ① wrote the letter that no reader in the office would have recorded, and he said the writing was the whole of the week. The ② letter, meaning the note itself and not the stamp, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a letter, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ letter in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ letter at the far box, meaning the page they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A letter, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the clerk said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the letter was the whole of the matter, meaning the word and not the note. The ⑥ letter, meaning the word and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; letter, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a note and a word. He said the word is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ letter had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ letter of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in September, was one office and three weeks of recording; letter, he said, is either the page at the far box or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ letter I remember is the note recorded in the register, which closed in 1967 and is still recorded as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ letter, my mother said in 1969, is the only note that improves by being recorded; every letter, she said, is a word that has agreed to look like a note. She said the word was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 信；字母（指邮局里每一封旁边的那一封）
B. n. 信；字母（指那封信本身，与邮票相对）
C. 固定搭配：write the letter 写这封信
D. n. 信；字母（指留给孩子们留着的那一页那一封）
E. n. 通信之事（抽象总称，指一处邮局的信之事）
F. n. 信；字母（指收发簿里写到、被记载的的那一封）
G. n. 话、音信（指一件事里人人都寄却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 音信（抽象总称，指人人都寄却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: wrote the letter that no reader in the office would have recorded
The letter, meaning the note itself and not the stamp
the letter at the far box
the letter was the whole of the matter
the letter had become a line in a register
The letter of the whole thing
A letter, my mother said in 1969

answers.why: write the letter 意为“写这封信”，1960 年那位文书把邮局里没有一位收信人肯记载的一封信做了一遍。
letter 意为“信；字母”，指那封信本身而不是邮票，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记载。
letter 意为“信；字母”，指邮局里每一封旁边的那一封，每一封旁边都有同一枚小小的邮票。
letter 意为“信；字母”，指最远那只信箱留给孩子们留着的那一页那一封，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
letter 意为“话、音信”，指一件事里人人都寄却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这句话就是那件事的全部。
letter 意为“音信”，指人人都寄却无人提起的那样东西而不是那封信，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
letter 意为“信；字母”，指收发簿里写到、被记载的的那一封，到 1965 年这一封成了收发簿里的一行。
letter 意为“通信之事”，文书九月写道，整件事的信之事是一处邮局和三个星期的记载。
letter 意为“信；字母”，我记得的是收发簿里记载过的那一封，1967 年寄出了，至今仍被说成邮局里最安静的一封。
letter 为抽象总称，母亲 1969 年说，信是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的信。
